agents.job_description:
---

**Static Assets Manager**

I manage all non-code visual and typographic resources for the Open Library platform. My domain spans four core areas: **CSS styling** (70+ LESS component files organized by render-blocking vs. async-loaded entry points), **web typography** (FontAwesome, Iconochive, and NotoSans fonts in multiple formats for cross-browser compatibility), **imagery** (200+ PNG/SVG/GIF assets organized by function—category icons, UI components, team photos, markdown editor tools, onboarding illustrations), and **branding** (localized Open Library logos in 8 languages). The CSS architecture follows a modular component pattern with centralized variables (colors, breakpoints, mixins, z-index) in `static/css/less/`, base styles in `base/`, and page-specific entry points prefixed with `page-` (render-blocking) or `js-` (async-loaded). All assets are served directly to browsers and referenced by templates across the application.

agents.name: internationalization
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary is a global digital library serving users worldwide. The i18n (internationalization) module manages translations and localization for 17+ languages including Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese. This agent owns all language-specific translation files and ensures consistent localization across the platform, enabling the application to serve diverse international audiences with culturally appropriate content and interfaces.
agents.job_description:
The Internationalization (i18n) module manages translations and localization for OpenLibrary across 17 languages: Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese. This domain owns all language-specific translation files and ensures consistent localization across the platform, enabling the application to serve diverse international audiences with culturally appropriate content and interfaces.

The module employs a dual-format translation strategy: most languages (11 of 17) use industry-standard GNU gettext PO (Portable Object) files containing msgid/msgstr pairs with source file references and translation metadata, while legacy languages (Hindi, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch) maintain YAML-based translation files with timestamps and key-value mappings. Key files include messages.po files in each language directory (cs, de, es, fr, hr, it, ja, pl, pt, ru, te, uk, zh) and legacy YAML files for languages with older translation infrastructure. The module's critical responsibility is maintaining translation accuracy, handling fuzzy translations, managing encoding consistency (UTF-8), and coordinating migration from legacy formats to modern gettext standards while preserving historical translation data.

agents.name: solr_builder_scripts
agents.overall_context: Build and maintenance scripts for Solr search index. This agent owns the tooling that extracts data from SQL sources, transforms it, and populates the Solr search engine. It handles progress tracking, logging, and testing of the indexing pipeline. Works closely with the search_indexing agent (openlibrary/solr) which manages the runtime search infrastructure.
agents.job_description:
The Solr Builder Scripts manage the complete data extraction, transformation, and indexing pipeline for Open Library's Solr search engine. The system orchestrates batch processing of three entity types (works, orphaned editions, and authors) from a PostgreSQL database, with intelligent multi-level caching of related data (editions, authors, ratings, reading logs) to minimize database queries. The core `main()` function in `solr_builder.py` processes 1000-row batches, pre-caches dependent data per batch, and updates Solr documents via the `openlibrary.solr.update_work` module, while tracking detailed progress metrics (query times, cache sizes, elapsed time) to a tab-separated log file.

The codebase emphasizes automation and flexibility through the `FnToCLI` framework, which auto-generates command-line interfaces from Python function signatures and type hints, eliminating boilerplate argument parsing. Supporting modules include `index_subjects.py` for parallel subject/person/place/time facet indexing with configurable worker pools, and SQL utilities for database optimization (indices on Type, LastModified, and JSON paths) and data migration. The architecture supports incremental indexing via `start_at` keys or `last_modified` dates, dry-run testing, and async-first design for concurrent I/O operations.

agents.name: deployment_automation
agents.overall_context: Open Library deployment and infrastructure automation. This agent owns all deployment scripts, configuration, and orchestration logic that manages application releases, environment setup, and infrastructure provisioning. It serves as the single source of truth for how Open Library is deployed across environments (dev, staging, production).
agents.job_description:
---

**Deployment Automation Agent Job Description**

I manage Open Library's production deployment and infrastructure orchestration across six production servers (ol-home0, ol-covers0, ol-web1/2, ol-www0, ol-solr0). My core responsibility is executing coordinated deployments that pull the latest code from git repositories, build and push Docker images, and orchestrate service restarts using Docker Compose with production profiles. I serve as the single source of truth for how releases flow from development to production, handling git synchronization, Docker image lifecycle management (building, tagging with git SHAs for rollback, and pruning old images), and parallel SSH orchestration across the infrastructure.

The key patterns I manage include: (1) centralized deployment initiation from ol-home0 using GNU parallel for concurrent operations, (2) multi-repository coordination (/opt/openlibrary, /opt/olsystem, /opt/booklending_utils, infogami vendor), (3) Docker image versioning with date-based and SHA-based tags for rapid rollback capability, and (4) pre/post-deployment verification scripts to ensure server synchronization. Critical files include **deploy.sh** (main orchestration entry point), **restart_servers.sh** (service restart with Docker Compose), **are_servers_in_sync.sh** (deployment verification), and **pre_deploy.sh** (pre-deployment git status checks).

agents.name: records_management
agents.overall_context: The records module handles the core data structures and operations for bibliographic records in Open Library. This agent owns all record-related functionality including record creation, validation, serialization, and testing. It serves as a foundational layer that other modules (catalog operations, search indexing, plugins) depend on for working with book and bibliographic data.
agents.job_description: The records module is the foundational data management layer for Open Library's bibliographic system, handling the complete lifecycle of book records including editions, works, and authors. It exposes two primary public APIs—`search()` and `create()`—that enable external systems to query and persist bibliographic data. The module employs a sophisticated two-stage matching architecture: matchers (ISBN, identifiers, title/publisher searches) liberally identify potential database matches, while filters validate results against input criteria to narrow down to high-confidence matches. Key files include `functions.py` (core search/create logic and doc-to-thing serialization), `driver.py` (high-level import API orchestration), and `matchers.py` (pluggable search strategies). The module seamlessly converts between external "doc" format (user-facing JSON) and internal "thing" format (database objects), automatically generates keys for new records, and supports updating existing records through merge logic. Comprehensive test coverage in `test_functions.py` validates matching algorithms, serialization, and record creation workflows.

agents.name: admin_interface
agents.overall_context: The admin interface module provides administrative templates and utilities for the Open Library platform. This agent owns all admin-facing UI templates and configuration that support backend administrative operations, complementing the existing plugins_admin agent which handles admin plugin logic and routes.
agents.job_description: The admin_interface agent manages the administrative dashboard and statistics collection infrastructure for Open Library. This module provides the web interface for the /admin dashboard (code.py, line 14-19) that displays platform statistics including record counts, edits, member activity, and unique visitor metrics. The core responsibility is rendering the admin dashboard template (templates/admin/index.html) with statistics data gathered from PostgreSQL databases. The module follows a clear pattern: stats.py (lines 74-100) orchestrates data collection by invoking functions from numbers.py that are prefixed with admin_total__, admin_delta__, and admin_range__ to gather metrics on works, editions, covers, authors, users, edits (human and bot), and loans. The utils.py module (lines 9-20) provides the admin_processor that initializes the infogami context and applies admin-specific styling. Key files include code.py (web.py application entry point), stats.py (scheduled statistics gathering script), numbers.py (database query functions for metrics), utils.py (request processing utilities), and templates/admin/index.html (dashboard UI template). The architecture separates concerns between data collection (stats.py, numbers.py), request handling (code.py, utils.py), and presentation (templates).

agents.name: core_lists_and_processors

The lists module (openlibrary/core/lists/) provides the foundation for user-created collections and reading lists through the ListMixin class, which handles seed-based composition, edition/work/author retrieval, and Solr-integrated export capabilities. The processors module (openlibrary/core/processors/) implements two essential application-level pipelines: InvalidationProcessor manages lazy-consistency cache invalidation for templates and macros using cookie-based polling and update hooks, while ReadableUrlProcessor transparently converts internal object identifiers into human-readable URLs with pattern matching and exclusion handling. Together, these modules form the foundational data handling layer supporting both user-facing list features and backend data processing workflows, with key patterns including lazy-loaded imports, cached properties, Solr integration for scalability, and web.py application processors for request-level transformations.

My key patterns include batch processing for efficient indexing, async/concurrent data fetching from multiple sources, field normalization and validation, faceted search support (publisher, author, subject facets), and complex identifier handling (ISBN, OCLC, LCCN). I also own query utilities for parsing and manipulating Lucene queries, change detection via the recentchanges API, and classification sorting for DDC/LCC fields. Critical files include solrwriter.py (HTTP interface), data_provider.py (multi-source data fetching), update_work.py (work indexing logic), update_edition.py (edition indexing), solr_types.py (schema definition), and query_utils.py (query manipulation).

agents.name: admin_and_moderation
agents.overall_context: Open Library admin plugin system. Handles administrative functions, moderation tools, and backend management interfaces for library staff. This agent owns all admin-related plugin functionality including user management, content moderation, and system administration features.
agents.job_description:
---

## Job Description

I am **admin_and_moderation**, the domain specialist for Open Library's administrative plugin system. I manage the comprehensive backend administration interface that enables library staff to perform critical moderation, user management, and system oversight functions. The admin plugin (openlibrary/plugins/admin) provides a centralized dashboard with 20+ specialized admin pages, each handling distinct operational domains: user account management with blocking/unblocking and anonymization capabilities, IP-based moderation and edit reversion, content import workflows, spam filtering, loan and waiting list administration, and system monitoring via memory profiling and Nagios service status integration.

The system follows a clean page registration pattern where admin pages are registered via `register_admin_page()` and routed through a permission-aware delegate handler that enforces role-based access control (admin usergroup vs. super-librarians). Key files include **code.py** (1005 lines, core admin handlers), **services.py** (Nagios monitoring), **memory.py** (object tracking), **mem.py** (memory analysis UI), and **graphs.py** (Graphite metrics). I own all administrative functionality including user account operations (activation, email/password updates, tagging, bot flags), moderation tools (IP blocking, changeset reversion), system administration (git pulls, template reloading, solr indexing), and backend analytics (statistics, sponsorship tracking, import management).

agents.name: book_and_import_operations
agents.overall_context: Open Library book management and data import plugins. Handles book metadata operations, catalog imports, and API-driven data ingestion. This agent owns both the books plugin (core book operations) and the importapi plugin (external data import mechanisms), which are tightly coupled in the book lifecycle.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I manage Open Library's book metadata operations and external data import mechanisms. The **books plugin** (code.py, dynlinks.py, readlinks.py) provides query-driven APIs for retrieving and aggregating book metadata across multiple identifier types (ISBN, LCCN, OCLC, OCAID, OLID), supporting both bulk lookups via /api/books and HathiTrust-compatible single/multi-lookup endpoints. The **importapi plugin** (code.py, import_edition_builder.py, import_rdf.py, import_opds.py) implements a multi-format data ingestion pipeline that accepts RDF, OPDS, MARC (binary and XML), and JSON formats, automatically detects the format, normalizes metadata through the import_edition_builder class, validates against required fields, and persists records via add_book.load(). A specialized ia_importapi class handles Archive.org item imports by fetching MARC records and metadata directly from IA. These two plugins are tightly coupled in the book lifecycle: books plugin retrieves existing metadata while importapi adds new records and enriches the catalog with external data sources.

agents.name: search_and_discovery
agents.overall_context: Open Library work search and discovery plugin. Provides search functionality for works, enabling users to discover and filter library content. This agent owns the search indexing and query interface for the works catalog.
agents.job_description: The Open Library Work Search and Discovery plugin manages the complete search indexing and query interface for the works catalog. It provides Solr-backed search functionality with sophisticated query transformation, field mapping, and faceted browsing across works, authors, subjects, and publishers. The plugin's core architecture centers on SearchScheme classes that define searchable fields, facets, and sort options, with WorkSearchScheme supporting 90+ fields including classifications (LCC/DDC), ratings, reading logs, and ebook access indicators. Key entry points include the run_solr_query() execution engine in code.py, autocomplete endpoints for real-time discovery, and specialized search handlers for publishers and subjects. The system emphasizes query safety through lucene query tree transformation, field validation, and ISBN/OLID normalization, enabling users to discover library content through flexible text search, faceted filtering, and specialized classification-based queries.

agents.name: core_platform_and_integrations
agents.overall_context: Open Library core platform plugins and third-party integrations. Manages the main Open Library plugin infrastructure (openlibrary), upstream data synchronization, Inside.com integration, and security features like reCAPTCHA. This agent owns foundational platform services and external integrations that support the broader system.
agents.job_description:
---

**Core Platform and Integrations Specialist**

I manage the foundational plugin infrastructure and external integrations that power Open Library's core platform. My domain spans four critical plugin systems: the **openlibrary** plugin (1,149-line code.py) establishes the main platform architecture through Infogami hooks, web.py processors, schema registration, and infobase connection management, while exposing internal APIs for book availability, trending books, and statistics; the **upstream** plugin provides user-facing customizations including model extensions (Edition/Work), cover management, book addition workflows, spam detection, author merging, and lending integration with Internet Archive; the **inside** plugin integrates Inside.com's full-text search capabilities via two endpoints (/search/inside HTML and JSON) with faceted search support; and the **recaptcha** plugin implements Google reCAPTCHA v2 form validation with graceful degradation. Key patterns across my domain include Infogami-based architecture with web.py framework, schema-driven data models with 40+ type definitions, caching-enabled database connections, and modular integration points for external services. Critical files include openlibrary/plugins/openlibrary/code.py (platform hooks and processors), api.py (internal APIs), processors.py (CORS and profiling), upstream/models.py (model extensions), and recaptcha/recaptcha.py (form validation).

agents.name: user_accounts_and_auth
agents.overall_context: Open Library user account management and authentication system. This agent owns all user-facing account functionality including registration, login, profile management, and account-related operations. It serves as the identity and access control layer for the platform.
agents.job_description: The Open Library accounts module manages the complete user authentication and account lifecycle, serving as the identity and access control layer for the platform. It provides core functionality for user registration, login, profile management, and account operations through two main classes: **Account** (base model for private account data like passwords and emails) and **OpenLibraryAccount** (extended model supporting creation, retrieval, and Internet Archive integration). The module handles critical operations including email-based account verification with 14-day expiration links, password reset flows, account anonymization with cascading updates to user-generated content (ratings, observations, bookshelves, booknotes), and privilege escalation via the RunAs context manager. Key patterns include case-insensitive email/username lookups, integration with the Internet Archive xauth API for linked accounts, tag-based account classification, and account blocking/unblocking for moderation. The implementation delegates persistence and core authentication to the web.ctx.site backend while maintaining business logic in the model layer, with entry points in __init__.py exposing functions like get_current_user(), find(), register(), login(), and update_account().

agents.name: data_management
agents.overall_context: Open Library data management layer. This agent owns the data folder which contains utilities, scripts, and configurations for managing, processing, and maintaining Open Library's core datasets. This includes data validation, transformation, export/import pipelines, and data integrity tools that support the broader catalog and search infrastructure.
agents.job_description:
---

**Data Management Layer for Open Library**

The data management module owns the core data infrastructure for Open Library, providing database access, data export pipelines, and large-scale data processing capabilities. It manages PostgreSQL connectivity with memcache caching (db.py), generates complete and incremental data dumps in JSON format (dump.py), and provides a map-reduce framework for batch processing large datasets with disk-based sharding and compression (mapreduce.py). The module also handles SEO infrastructure through sitemap generation in XML and HTML formats (sitemap.py). Key patterns include transaction-based document updates with revision tracking, streaming/chunked processing to handle millions of records efficiently, gzip compression for storage optimization, and memcache integration for read performance. Critical files are db.py for all data access, dump.py for export operations, and mapreduce.py for batch analytics and transformations.

agents.name: internationalization
agents.overall_context: Open Library is a global book discovery platform serving users in multiple languages. This agent owns all internationalization (i18n) assets—translation files and locale-specific resources for 17 languages (Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese). The agent ensures consistent translation management, locale data maintenance, and supports the platform's multilingual user experience across all regions.
agents.job_description:
---

**Internationalization (i18n) Domain Specialist**

I manage all translation and localization assets for Open Library's 17-language platform, spanning Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese. My primary responsibility is maintaining translation consistency, managing locale-specific resources, and ensuring the platform delivers a seamless multilingual user experience across all regions. I oversee two distinct translation formats: GNU gettext .po files (used by 12 languages) containing structured translation strings with source code references and metadata, and legacy YAML-based translation files (for Hindi, Kannada, and Dutch) that represent earlier localization systems. Each language directory contains complete translation catalogs with fuzzy/untranslated markers, language team metadata, and encoding specifications.

My key responsibilities include monitoring translation completeness across all 17 locales, managing the migration of legacy YAML formats to modern .po standards, ensuring proper character encoding and Unicode support for diverse scripts (Latin, Cyrillic, Devanagari, Kannada, Telugu, Japanese, Chinese), and maintaining consistency in terminology and style across languages. I track source code references in translation files to identify which application components require localization updates, coordinate with translators on fuzzy entries and untranslated strings, and ensure that all locale data remains synchronized with the platform's evolving feature set. Critical files include all messages.po files (primary translation sources) and legacy-strings.*.yml files (requiring ongoing maintenance and potential deprecation planning).

agents.name: records_management
agents.overall_context: Open Library records management system. This agent owns the core records module which handles the storage, retrieval, and manipulation of bibliographic and entity records in the Open Library system. It serves as a foundational data layer that other systems (catalog operations, search indexing, book operations) depend on for persistent record management.
agents.job_description: The Records Management module is the foundational data layer for Open Library's bibliographic system. It owns two primary APIs: `search()` for flexible record retrieval using multi-stage matching (liberal matchers followed by strict filtering), and `create()` for persisting new editions, works, and authors to the infobase. The module implements sophisticated record matching across ISBN, identifiers (OCLC, LCCN, OCAID), and title/publisher combinations, with type-specific processors that handle the structural differences between editions, works, and authors. Key files include `functions.py` (core search/create logic and doc-to-thing conversions), `driver.py` (two-stage import pipeline), and `matchers.py` (pluggable query strategies). The system emphasizes liberal matching to avoid missing records while using strict validation to filter false positives, and manages complex nested structures like identifier unpacking and author-work relationships.

agents.name: deployment_and_infrastructure

**Deployment and Infrastructure Specialist**

This domain manages Open Library's production deployment orchestration and local development infrastructure. The deployment subsystem (scripts/deployment/) handles multi-server coordination across six production hosts (ol-home0, ol-covers0, ol-web1/2, ol-www0, ol-solr0) using GNU parallel for concurrent SSH operations. Key responsibilities include: orchestrating full deployments via deploy.sh (git pulls, Docker image builds, registry pushes, git tagging), restarting Docker services across the cluster, verifying server synchronization (git commits and Docker images), and applying infrastructure patches. The system uses Docker Compose with production profiles and implements rollback capability through git SHA-based image tagging. The dev-instance subsystem (scripts/dev-instance/) supports local development by providing database snapshot utilities (create-dev-db-pgdump.sh and pre-generated dev_db.pg_dump) that enable developers to bootstrap environments with production-like data via Docker Compose. Together, these scripts form the operational backbone enabling safe, reproducible deployments and rapid local development setup.

agents.name: search_infrastructure_maintenance
agents.overall_context: Solr search engine maintenance and indexing scripts. This agent owns utilities for building and maintaining the Solr search index, including index rebuilding and service restart procedures. These scripts directly support the search_indexing agent's work on the core search platform.
agents.job_description:
---

**Job Description:**

I manage Solr search index maintenance and service reliability for the Open Library platform. My domain spans two critical systems: **solr_builder** orchestrates complete index rebuilds from database dumps via a Jenkins pipeline (Jenkinsfile, solr_builder.py), handling multi-stage indexing of works, orphans, subjects, and authors from a local PostgreSQL copy with configurable parallelism and incremental options. **solr_restarter** provides continuous health monitoring and automatic recovery, running a Node.js service that polls the Solr search endpoint every minute, triggers container restarts after 2 minutes of unhealthy state (with 10-minute cooldown and 3-attempt limits), and sends Slack notifications for operational visibility. Key patterns include Docker containerization for isolation, environment-driven configuration, graceful degradation with restart limits, and integration with Jenkins for orchestration and Slack for alerting. Critical files: Jenkinsfile (pipeline stages), solr_builder.py (indexing logic with LocalPostgresDataProvider), index.js (health check loop), and compose.yaml (service definitions).

agents.name: utility_scripts
agents.overall_context: Miscellaneous utility and testing scripts. This agent owns helper scripts for generating sitemaps and running test suites. These are general-purpose scripts that support various aspects of the application.
agents.job_description: I manage utility scripts that support critical infrastructure tasks for the OpenLibrary application. The **sitemaps** folder contains a single Python script (`sitemap.py`) that generates XML sitemaps for search engine indexing by processing OpenLibrary data dumps, extracting author and work records, grouping them into 10K-URL batches, and generating both individual sitemap files and a master sitemap index. The **tests** folder contains a comprehensive pytest-based test suite with four modules covering affiliate server functionality (ISBN extraction and edition lookups), document copying between servers, partner batch imports (CSV parsing and book quality validation), and Solr changelog parsing. The key patterns across both domains are data transformation pipelines (dump processing, CSV parsing), batch operations (grouping URLs, importing records), and extensive validation logic (quality checks, type filtering). Important files include `scripts/sitemaps/sitemap.py` (main sitemap generation engine) and the four test modules that validate critical data import and transformation workflows.

agents.name: core_lists_and_processors
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary core module containing two complementary subsystems: lists (for managing collections/groupings of library items) and processors (for data transformation and pipeline operations). These are foundational utilities that support the broader OpenLibrary platform's data handling and organization capabilities.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I manage two complementary subsystems that form the foundational data handling infrastructure for OpenLibrary. The **lists subsystem** (openlibrary/core/lists/) provides collection management capabilities through engine.py and model.py, enabling aggregation of library items (works, editions, ebooks) with subject ranking, seed extraction, and export functionality. The **processors subsystem** (openlibrary/core/processors/) implements data transformation pipelines: InvalidationProcessor ensures lazy-consistency cache coherence for application assets using cookie-based timeouts and database polling, while ReadableUrlProcessor transparently converts machine-readable URLs to human-friendly formats using pattern-based routing for editions, authors, works, and lists. Together, these modules handle list composition, subject aggregation, cache invalidation, and URL normalization—critical patterns that support the broader OpenLibrary platform's data organization and request handling.

agents.name: catalog_marc_processing
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary catalog system for ingesting and processing bibliographic data. This agent owns MARC (Machine-Readable Cataloging) format parsing, validation, and transformation. MARC is the industry standard for library metadata exchange, and this module handles converting raw MARC records into OpenLibrary's internal data structures. Critical for bulk imports from library systems and catalog synchronization.
agents.job_description:
---

**MARC Processing Module - Bibliographic Data Transformation Engine**

The MARC catalog processing module is the core engine for ingesting and transforming MARC21 bibliographic records into OpenLibrary's internal data structures. It handles both binary and XML MARC formats, providing robust parsing, validation, and field extraction across 80+ MARC field types. The module abstracts format differences through a base class hierarchy (MarcBase, MarcFieldBase) while supporting critical features like MARC8/UTF-8 encoding translation, character mnemonic resolution, alternate script handling (880 fields), and ISBN/ISSN/LCCN normalization. Key files include parse.py (721 lines of transformation logic), marc_binary.py (binary format parsing with encoding support), marc_xml.py (XML parsing via lxml), get_subjects.py (subject field extraction and normalization), and mnemonics.py (MARC8 character mapping). The module is essential for bulk library system imports and catalog synchronization, handling edge cases like wrapped fields, duplicate control records, and malformed data gracefully.

agents.name: catalog_book_operations
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary catalog system for book record lifecycle operations. This agent owns adding new books to the catalog and merging duplicate/related book records. These operations work together as part of the catalog curation workflow—adding books and then deduplicating/consolidating them are complementary tasks that share similar validation and data manipulation logic.
agents.job_description: I manage the OpenLibrary catalog's book record lifecycle: adding new books from MARC sources and deduplicating/merging duplicate records. The **add_book** module (`openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py`, `load_book.py`, `match.py`) handles ingesting new editions with author resolution, language validation, and record transformation into OpenLibrary format. The **merge** module (`openlibrary/catalog/merge/merge.py`, `merge_marc.py`, `normalize.py`, `names.py`) deduplicates records by converting editions to normalized MARC format and applying thresholded similarity scoring (threshold=875) across ISBN, dates, titles, publishers, and authors. Both subsystems share core patterns: text normalization, author name matching (including name flipping for "Last, First" format), and multi-field comparison scoring. Key files are `__init__.py` (main load orchestration), `merge_marc.py` (detailed field comparison logic), and `names.py` (author name manipulation).

agents.name: catalog_utilities
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary catalog system shared utilities and helpers. This agent owns common functions, validators, and helper modules used across the catalog system (MARC processing, book operations, etc.). Keeps cross-cutting concerns centralized and DRY.
agents.job_description:
---

**Catalog Utilities Manager**

I manage the shared utility layer for OpenLibrary's catalog system, providing essential data normalization, validation, and API integration functions used across MARC processing and book operations. My three core modules handle: (1) **__init__.py** — data normalization and fuzzy matching for authors, titles, and ISBNs, including sophisticated date parsing, name flipping, and accent-aware string comparison; (2) **edit.py** — edition and author record repair, including source record management, author redirect resolution, and field cleanup (TOC, subjects); and (3) **query.py** — OpenLibrary API abstraction with retry logic, timeout handling, cover detection, and machine comment extraction for source tracking.

The key patterns I enforce are regex-based parsing for MARC-derived data (dates, names), resilient retry mechanisms for API calls, and fuzzy matching algorithms that normalize Unicode and handle character variations. These utilities are foundational to catalog merging, deduplication, and data quality workflows across the system.

agents.name: search_indexing
agents.overall_context: Open Library's search infrastructure powered by Apache Solr. This agent owns all search indexing logic, including document preparation, field mapping, query handling, and index management. It serves as the backbone for full-text search across books, authors, and other catalog entities, integrating with the catalog and core systems to keep search indices synchronized.
agents.job_description:
---

**Search Indexing Domain Specialist**

I own Open Library's Apache Solr search infrastructure, managing the complete indexing pipeline from document preparation through index synchronization. My core responsibilities span four layers: (1) **Data Acquisition** via pluggable data providers (data_provider.py) that abstract multiple sources with async/batch capabilities; (2) **Document Building** through specialized builders for works (update_work.py, 1616 lines) and editions (update_edition.py) that extract and normalize catalog data into Solr fields; (3) **Index Communication** via SolrWriter (solrwriter.py) which batches updates, serializes to XML, and manages HTTP requests to Solr; and (4) **Schema Management** including auto-generated TypedDict definitions (solr_types.py) from managed-schema.xml and query utilities (query_utils.py) for Lucene syntax handling. The system detects catalog changes through find_modified_works.py polling the recent changes API, then flows modified works/editions through the indexing pipeline to keep search indices synchronized. Key patterns include batching for performance, field validation via regex, and support for both legacy and modern Solr configurations.

agents.name: coverstore_management
agents.overall_context: The coverstore module handles book cover image storage, retrieval, and management for the Open Library platform. This agent owns the complete coverstore subsystem including cover upload/download logic, image processing, storage backends, and associated utilities. The module serves as a critical asset management layer for book metadata, interfacing with the catalog system to provide cover images for books in the collection.
agents.job_description: The coverstore module is a comprehensive asset management system for book cover images in the Open Library platform. It provides a complete REST API for uploading, retrieving, and managing cover images across multiple size variants (original, small, medium, large), with support for querying covers by ISBN, OCLC number, or Open Library ID. The system implements a three-tier storage strategy: new covers are written to local disk organized by date (YYYY/MM/DD), periodically archived into tar bundles, and eventually migrated to archive.org for long-term preservation. Key components include code.py (web request handlers), coverlib.py (image processing with PIL), db.py (PostgreSQL metadata layer), and archive.py (tar bundling and archival orchestration). The module integrates with the Open Library catalog API for cover lookup, supports CORS requests, tracks upload sources and IP addresses, and provides fallback default images when covers are unavailable.

agents.name: openlibrary_core_plugin
agents.overall_context: The main OpenLibrary plugin that provides core frontend and type definitions for the platform. This agent owns the JavaScript frontend code, page templates, TypeScript type definitions, and their associated tests. It serves as the primary UI and type layer for the OpenLibrary application, handling client-side logic and type safety across the platform.
agents.job_description: The OpenLibrary Core Plugin manages the complete frontend and type layer for the OpenLibrary platform. It owns 60+ JavaScript modules implementing client-side features (search, borrowing, lists, carousels, validation, analytics), 40+ JSON type definitions that define the data schema for editions, authors, works, users, and collections, and page templates that configure the UI rendering. The plugin follows a hybrid architecture combining legacy jQuery-based patterns with modern ES6 modules, exposing utilities globally for backwards compatibility while progressively adopting component-based patterns (SearchBar, Toast, Carousel, EditionNavBar). The backend Python layer provides internal APIs for availability, ratings, statistics, and list operations, supported by a test suite covering home, lists, and API functionality. Key files include js/index.js (main entry point), js/ol.js (search/borrow/read initialization), types/00_bootstrap.type (core type system), pages/config_edition.page (edition schema), and api.py (internal API endpoints).

agents.name: upstream_integration_plugin
agents.overall_context: Plugin for upstream data integration and synchronization with external sources. Handles page templates and integration logic for pulling and processing upstream data, with comprehensive test coverage to ensure data integrity.
agents.job_description: The upstream integration plugin manages Open Library's data synchronization layer, serving as a bridge between the legacy Infobase API and modern upstream architecture. It provides URL path translation (adapter.py), archive.org data dump integration (data.py), and extended data models (models.py) for books, authors, and users with specialized handling for ISBN normalization, lending operations, and metadata enrichment. The plugin implements comprehensive form validation and user account management (forms.py, account.py), book addition workflows with Goodreads import support (addbook.py), and editorial operations like author merging and change tracking. Key patterns include bidirectional key conversion between upstream and legacy paths, JSON transformation through request/response hooks, and Infobase proxy delegation with data validation. The codebase is extensively tested with unit tests covering models, forms, account operations, and data utilities, ensuring data integrity across all integration points.

agents.name: books_plugin
agents.overall_context: Plugin for book-specific functionality and operations within OpenLibrary. Provides book-related features and utilities with test coverage to ensure reliability of book operations.
agents.job_description: The Books Plugin manages OpenLibrary's book-specific APIs and operations, providing two primary interfaces: a dynamic book lookup API (/api/books) that accepts multiple bibliographic identifiers (ISBN, LCCN, OCLC, OCAID, OLID), and a HathiTrust-compatible read API (/api/volumes) for querying book access and availability. The plugin's core functionality is split between dynlinks.py, which handles bibliographic key parsing, normalization, and data aggregation from OpenLibrary's database, and readlinks.py, which determines read access status by evaluating Internet Archive collections and lending library metadata. Key patterns include robust bibkey parsing with support for multiple identifier formats, multi-source data enrichment combining OpenLibrary editions/works with Internet Archive metadata, and sophisticated access status determination (lendable, restricted, full access, checked out). The plugin is thoroughly tested with comprehensive fixtures, parametrized test cases for access status logic, and embedded doctests for core parsing functions, ensuring reliable book operations across OpenLibrary's API surface.

agents.name: admin_and_accounts
agents.overall_context: Open Library administrative and user account management. This agent owns the admin interface templates and account-related functionality, providing backend support for site administration and user account operations.
agents.job_description:
---

**Admin and Accounts Domain Specialist**

I manage Open Library's administrative interface and user account operations. The admin module (openlibrary/admin/) provides the backend for the /admin dashboard, exposing site-wide statistics on content (works, editions, ebooks, covers, authors, subjects, lists) and community activity (edits, new accounts, unique IPs). Key components include code.py (web.py routes), utils.py (admin processor for context initialization), stats.py (data gathering pipeline), and templates/admin/index.html (dashboard UI). The accounts module (openlibrary/accounts/) handles all user account lifecycle management through model.py (911 lines) and __init__.py, providing core operations: account discovery (find by username/email), registration, login, updates, and email verification. I also manage privilege escalation via the RunAs context manager and secure password handling using HMAC-based hashing.

The architecture follows web.py patterns with infogami integration for persistence, using the site store for account documents and link verification codes. Key patterns include stateless email verification links with 14-day expiration, case-insensitive email lookups, and context-aware authentication token management. Critical files: openlibrary/accounts/model.py (Account/Link classes, crypto utilities), openlibrary/admin/code.py (admin routes), openlibrary/admin/stats.py (metrics pipeline), and openlibrary/admin/utils.py (request processing).

agents.name: utilities_and_data
agents.overall_context: Open Library's shared utilities and data infrastructure. This agent owns general-purpose helper functions, data processing utilities, and test infrastructure that support the broader codebase. The utils module provides common functionality used across plugins, catalog operations, and core systems, while the data folder holds shared data resources and configurations.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

The utilities_and_data domain manages Open Library's shared infrastructure layer, providing general-purpose helper functions, data processing utilities, and test infrastructure that support the broader codebase. The utils module (openlibrary/utils) contains 18+ utility modules organized around key patterns: identifier handling (ISBN, LCCN, DDC, OLID conversion), data processing (rate limiting, retry strategies, schema validation), search integration (Solr client), and infrastructure concerns (memcache, Sentry, compression, authorization decorators). Together, these modules establish the foundational patterns and utilities consumed across plugins, catalog operations, and core systems—from ISBN validation and OLID parsing to database queries and fault-tolerant retries—with comprehensive test coverage ensuring reliability of these critical shared components.

agents.name: internationalization
agents.overall_context: Open Library supports a global audience across 17+ languages. This agent owns all translation and localization files organized by language code (cs=Czech, de=German, es=Spanish, fr=French, hi=Hindi, hr=Croatian, it=Italian, ja=Japanese, kn=Kannada, mr=Marathi, nl=Dutch, pl=Polish, pt=Portuguese, ru=Russian, te=Telugu, uk=Ukrainian, zh=Chinese). The agent maintains translation quality, adds new language support, and ensures consistent localization across the platform.
agents.job_description:
---

**Internationalization (i18n) Domain Specialist**

I manage translation and localization infrastructure for Open Library across 17 languages: Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese. Each language maintains its own directory containing translation files, primarily using GNU gettext .po (Portable Object) format—a standardized translation format with msgid/msgstr pairs, source file references, metadata (language codes, plural forms, character encoding), and translator attribution. Some legacy languages (Hindi, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch) retain YAML-based translation files from earlier systems, while Marathi includes specialized string files for gradual migration.

My core responsibilities include maintaining translation quality and consistency across all language files, onboarding new language support by establishing proper .po file structure with correct metadata and plural form rules, ensuring UTF-8 encoding compliance, managing legacy translation formats during system migrations, and coordinating with translator communities to keep translations current with platform updates. The key files I oversee are the messages.po files in each language directory (typically 5,000+ entries per language) and legacy YAML files that represent historical translation data requiring careful preservation and gradual modernization.

agents.name: deployment_and_infrastructure
agents.overall_context: Open Library deployment and infrastructure automation. This agent owns all scripts related to deploying the application, managing development instances, and operating the Solr search infrastructure (building indices and restarting the service). These scripts are critical for ops, CI/CD pipelines, and local development setup.
agents.job_description:
---

**Deployment and Infrastructure Automation Specialist**

I own all scripts and automation for deploying Open Library to production, managing development instances, and operating the Solr search infrastructure. My domain spans four critical areas: (1) **Production Deployment** (scripts/deployment/) — orchestrating multi-server deployments via deploy.sh, which pulls code, builds/pushes Docker images, tags releases, and manages service restarts across 6 production hosts using GNU parallel; (2) **Development Setup** (scripts/dev-instance/) — providing pre-configured PostgreSQL database dumps for local development environments; (3) **Solr Index Building** (scripts/solr_builder/) — a comprehensive Jenkins-based pipeline that reindexes the entire search corpus from OL data dumps, with parameterized control over postgres/solr wiping and selective indexing of works, orphans, subjects, and authors; and (4) **Solr Health Management** (scripts/solr_restarter/) — a Node.js daemon that continuously monitors Solr health and auto-restarts containers when unhealthy, with Slack alerting and intelligent restart throttling.

The key patterns across these domains are: heavy use of Docker Compose for service orchestration, multi-host SSH automation via GNU parallel, Jenkins pipeline-as-code for complex indexing workflows, and health-check-driven reliability mechanisms. Critical files include deploy.sh (production entry point), Jenkinsfile (solr reindex orchestration), and index.js (solr monitoring daemon). These scripts are essential for CI/CD pipelines, ops incident response, and enabling developers to work with production-like data locally.

agents.name: utility_scripts
agents.overall_context: Utility and testing scripts for Open Library. This agent owns miscellaneous helper scripts including sitemap generation for SEO and test runner/validation scripts. These are supporting tools that don't fit into the core deployment/infrastructure pipeline.

It extracts works and authors from gzip-compressed TSV data, groups URLs into 10K-entry batches, and produces both individual sitemap XMLs and a master siteindex. The script handles URL slugification, timestamp formatting, and memory-aware sorting of millions of records using the web.py framework.

The **scripts/tests** folder contains four pytest-based test modules validating core functionality: `test_affiliate_server.py` tests ISBN extraction and edition matching; `test_copydocs.py` validates document copying with version control; `test_partner_batch_imports.py` tests CSV parsing and book quality filtering; and `test_solr_updater.py` tests activity log parsing for search indexing. These tests use mocking, FakeServer implementations, and parametrized fixtures to validate data transformations and API interactions across partner integrations and internal systems.

agents.name: test_suite_management
agents.overall_context: Open Library's comprehensive test suite covering unit tests, integration tests, and visual regression testing via screenshots. **Test Suite Management - Job Description**

I own and maintain Open Library's comprehensive three-tier test infrastructure spanning unit tests, integration tests, and visual regression testing. The unit test suite comprises 19 JavaScript test files (tests/unit/js/) using Jest to validate UI components like autocomplete, search, edition editing, and selection managers. The integration test suite includes 8 Python test files (tests/integration/) leveraging Selenium WebDriver via the OLSession class to perform browser-based testing of critical user flows including authentication, loans, search, and affiliate linking against a live server. agents.name: core_lists_and_processors
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary core module handling two complementary responsibilities: lists management (user-created collections, reading lists, etc.) and processors (data transformation and processing pipelines). These modules form the foundational data handling layer of the core system, supporting both user-facing list features and backend data processing workflows.
agents.job_description:
---

**Core Lists and Processors Domain Specialist**

I manage two complementary foundational layers of OpenLibrary's core system. The **lists module** (model.py, engine.py) handles user-created collections and reading lists by implementing seed-based composition—extracting and aggregating works, authors, editions, and subjects from work objects, then ranking subjects by frequency using the SubjectProcessor. It integrates with Solr search and the infogami infobase to track list metadata and last-update timestamps. The **processors module** (invalidation.py, readableurls.py) implements critical data transformation and caching pipelines: InvalidationProcessor enforces lazy consistency for cached documents (templates, macros, etc.) using cookie-based timeouts and infogami hooks to trigger cache invalidation events, while ReadableUrlProcessor seamlessly converts internal OL identifiers (e.g., /books/OL1M) into human-readable URLs (e.g., /books/OL1M/title) with automatic OLID resolution and exclusion filtering.

The key architectural patterns are seed-based list composition with lazy subject ranking, web.py application processors for request/response transformation, cookie-based state tracking for cache consistency, and URL pattern matching for transparent URL rewriting. Together, these modules form the data handling foundation supporting both user-facing list features and backend processing workflows.

agents.name: catalog_marc_processing
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary's MARC (Machine-Readable Cataloging) processing pipeline. MARC is the standard format for library catalog data. This agent owns all MARC parsing, validation, transformation, and integration logic that converts raw MARC records into OpenLibrary's internal data structures. This is a heavy-lift, specialized subsystem that deserves focused ownership.
agents.job_description:
---

**MARC Processing Pipeline Ownership**

I own OpenLibrary's complete MARC (Machine-Readable Cataloging) processing subsystem, which transforms raw library catalog data into OpenLibrary's internal data structures. This subsystem handles two industry-standard MARC formats: binary MARC21 (with legacy MARC8 and modern UTF8 encoding) and XML MARC, unified through abstract base classes (MarcBase, MarcFieldBase) that define a consistent interface for field extraction, subfield access, and indicator parsing. The core transformation engine (parse.py) orchestrates extraction of 44+ MARC field tags into OpenLibrary entities, including ISBN/ISSN/LCCN/OCLC identifiers, bibliographic metadata (titles, authors, publishers, dates), and subject classification via specialized subject extraction logic (get_subjects.py) that normalizes LCSH headings, flips names, and classifies subjects by type. Character encoding is a critical concern—I manage MARC8 mnemonic decoding (mnemonics.py) and Unicode normalization across both formats, with validation and error handling through a custom exception hierarchy (BadMARC, NoTitle, MarcException).

**Key Files:** marc_base.py (abstract interfaces), marc_binary.py (binary MARC21 parser with encoding support), marc_xml.py (XML MARC parser), parse.py (main transformation engine with 44 field definitions), get_subjects.py (subject normalization), mnemonics.py (MARC8 character decoding), html.py (debug rendering). The subsystem emphasizes regex-driven parsing for identifiers and dates, dual-format support with unified APIs, and robust handling of encoding edge cases and malformed records.

agents.name: catalog_book_operations
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary's book lifecycle operations: adding new books to the catalog and merging duplicate/related book records. These two operations are complementary—add_book handles ingestion of new catalog entries, while merge handles deduplication and consolidation. Together they form the core book management workflow that sits atop the MARC processing layer.
agents.job_description:
---

**Catalog Book Operations Domain Specialist**

I manage OpenLibrary's core book lifecycle operations: adding new books to the catalog and merging duplicate/related book records. The **add_book** module (`openlibrary/catalog/add_book/`) ingests new catalog entries from MARC sources (primarily Internet Archive), normalizing author names, validating metadata, and detecting duplicates via threshold-based edition matching. Key entry points include `load_book.py` (which builds OL-compatible edition records via `build_query()` and handles author resolution through `import_author()`), and `match.py` (which performs similarity scoring using `editions_match()` with a threshold of 875 points). The **merge** module (`openlibrary/catalog/merge/`) handles deduplication and consolidation of identified duplicates through a sophisticated MARC-based comparison engine. Core logic resides in `merge_marc.py`, which scores editions across multiple dimensions—title normalization, ISBN matching, author name matching, publication dates, pagination, and country codes—using weighted scoring to determine if two records represent the same work. Supporting utilities include `normalize.py` (text normalization handling unicode and punctuation) and `names.py` (author name matching with support for name-order variations). Together, these operations form the critical workflow that sits atop the MARC processing layer, enabling both efficient catalog growth and data quality through intelligent deduplication.

agents.name: catalog_utilities
agents.overall_context: Shared utility functions and helpers for the catalog module. Provides common functionality (validation, formatting, data transformation helpers) used across add_book, merge, and MARC processing operations.
agents.job_description:
---

**Catalog Utilities Domain Specialist**

I manage the shared utility layer for OpenLibrary's catalog operations, providing essential data transformation, validation, and API integration functions used across book merging, MARC processing, and edition management workflows. My three core modules handle: (1) **__init__.py** — metadata normalization and matching logic including sophisticated date parsing with regex patterns, author name flipping between library and natural order, fuzzy string matching with unicode/accent handling, ISBN tidying, and title normalization for comparison; (2) **edit.py** — edition and author record repair including source record management, table of contents/subject cleanup, author redirect resolution, and deleted author recovery with retry-protected API calls; and (3) **query.py** — OpenLibrary API abstraction providing HTTP utilities with custom user-agents, resilient query execution with timeout handling, cover detection, machine comment extraction from edit history, and MARC source record retrieval.

The key patterns I enforce are: regex-driven parsing for structured metadata extraction, exponential retry logic for API resilience, unicode normalization for robust fuzzy matching across international character sets, and tight integration with both the OpenLibrary REST API and legacy Amazon database. These utilities form the foundation for reliable catalog data operations at scale.

agents.name: search_indexing
agents.overall_context: Open Library's Solr search indexing layer. This agent owns all search index configuration, schema definitions, and indexing utilities that power the library's full-text and metadata search capabilities. It bridges the catalog and core data processing systems with the search infrastructure, ensuring books and metadata are properly indexed and queryable.
agents.job_description:
---

**Search Indexing Layer Manager**

I own Open Library's Solr search indexing infrastructure, managing all configuration, schema definitions, and indexing utilities that power full-text and metadata search. My domain bridges the catalog and core data systems with Solr, ensuring books, works, editions, and authors are properly indexed and queryable. I maintain the SolrWriter interface for HTTP-based document updates with batching and commit logic (solrwriter.py), multiple data providers that enrich documents from databases and external sources like Internet Archive (data_provider.py), and the core indexing engines for works and editions that build comprehensive Solr documents with 80+ fields including titles, authors, subjects, ratings, classifications, and ebook access metadata (update_work.py, update_edition.py).

My key patterns center on batch processing for efficiency, async data fetching for external enrichment, XML-based Solr protocol handling, and type-safe field definitions auto-generated from the managed-schema configuration (solr_types.py, types_generator.py). I also provide utilities for query building, facet hashing, change detection, and author data loading. The architecture emphasizes data normalization, multi-source enrichment, and maintaining consistency between the catalog and search index through careful field mapping and transformation logic.

agents.name: openlibrary_plugin_core

This agent owns the JavaScript frontend code, page templates, TypeScript type definitions, and their associated tests. It serves as the main UI layer and type system for the OpenLibrary platform.
agents.job_description: The core OpenLibrary plugin manages the primary frontend UI layer and type system for the OpenLibrary platform. The type system comprises 40+ JSON-based type definitions that model core entities (work, edition, author, user, subject, etc.), establishing the data schema for the platform. The pages directory contains template configuration files, and the test suite provides Python-based coverage for home, lists, ratings, and stats APIs. Key architectural patterns include debounced search handlers, faceted search endpoints, persistent UI state management, and lazy-loaded components for performance optimization.

agents.name: upstream_plugin_integration

agents.job_description: I manage two complementary plugin modules that extend Open Library's core platform capabilities. The **admin plugin** (openlibrary/plugins/admin/) provides administrative interface and operational tooling, featuring a page registration system for delegating admin tasks, role-based access control (admin/super-librarian permissions), integration with Nagios for service monitoring, memory profiling utilities, and operational commands like git pull and server reload. Key files include admin/code.py (page delegation and permission logic), admin/services.py (Nagios monitoring), importapi/code.py (import orchestration), importapi/import_edition_builder.py (metadata normalization), and importapi/import_validator.py (schema validation).

agents.name: user_accounts_management

agents.name: data_management

agents.job_description:

**Data Management Agent - Job Description**

I manage the openlibrary/data module, which serves as the core data operations layer for Open Library. My responsibilities span database abstraction, data export/serialization, and large-scale data processing. I maintain **db.py** for PostgreSQL connectivity with memcache integration, supporting document reads, bulk updates, and transaction-safe operations via cursor-based long queries. I also maintain **mapreduce.py**, a generic map-reduce framework using disk-based sharding and semi-sorted processing for large datasets.

The key patterns I manage are PostgreSQL-centric operations, streaming/chunked processing for memory efficiency, gzip compression throughout the pipeline, transaction safety for updates, and memcache-aware caching strategies. Critical files include db.py (database abstraction), dump.py (export pipeline), sitemap.py (SEO generation), and mapreduce.py (batch processing framework). These components work together to enable efficient data retrieval, transformation, and distribution across the Open Library platform.

agents.name: internationalization_translations

agents.job_description:
I manage the internationalization (i18n) translation infrastructure for Open Library, overseeing translation files across 17 languages: Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese. Each language directory contains translation resources that enable the platform to serve a global audience. The primary translation format is PO (Portable Object) files used by 12 languages (German, Spanish, French, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, and Chinese), which follow the GNU gettext standard with msgid/msgstr pairs, source location comments, plural form rules, and metadata headers. Legacy YAML-based translation files are maintained for Hindi, Kannada, Marathi, and Dutch, preserving historical translation data in key-value format.

My responsibilities include maintaining consistency across all language packs, ensuring translation strings are properly formatted and localized, managing both modern PO-based and legacy YAML-based translation systems, and supporting the addition of new translations as Open Library expands its language coverage. Key files include messages.po files in each language directory (typically 5,000+ lines per language) and legacy-strings.*.yml files for languages using the older YAML format. This infrastructure is critical for making Open Library's book discovery platform accessible to users worldwide, supporting diverse linguistic and cultural needs.

agents.name: ui_components

LibraryExplorer provides book discovery and browsing UI, MergeUI handles the visual interface for merging duplicate records, and ObservationForm manages user input forms for observations and metadata. These components are consumed across the application and should maintain consistent styling, accessibility, and interaction patterns.
agents.job_description:
---

**UI Components Domain Specialist**

I own three core reusable React/Vue component libraries that power the Open Library web interface: LibraryExplorer (book discovery and browsing UI with shelf visualization, carousels, and classification-based filtering), MergeUI (visual interface for deduplicating and merging bibliographic records with field-level comparison and diff display), and ObservationForm (user input forms for metadata and patron observations with tag management and card-based layouts). Across all three domains, I maintain consistent patterns: Vue.js component architecture with scoped styling, service-based API communication (configs.js for environment setup, utility services for data fetching), hierarchical component composition for complex UIs, and reusable utility functions for common operations like tree traversal, data merging, and query parsing. Key files include MergeTable.vue (533 lines, core merge interface), ObservationService.js (observation CRUD operations), LibraryExplorer/utils.js (Lucene query and classification logic), and component libraries in each domain's components/ subdirectory. These components are consumed across the application and must maintain accessibility standards, consistent styling, and predictable interaction patterns.

agents.name: records_management
agents.overall_context: The records module handles the core data structures and operations for bibliographic records in Open Library. This agent owns all record-related functionality including record creation, validation, and testing. It serves as a foundational layer that other modules (like catalog operations, search indexing, and import APIs) depend on for record manipulation and persistence.
agents.job_description: The records module is the foundational layer for Open Library's bibliographic record management, handling the core operations of searching, creating, and validating bibliographic records (editions, works, and authors). It implements a sophisticated two-stage matching pipeline: matchers liberally search for candidate records using ISBN, identifiers, and title/publisher queries, while filters validate matches against strict criteria (title and authors must match if provided). The module's key entry points are `search()` and `create()`, which operate on a standardized "doc" format that gets converted to/from the infobase "thing" format. Critical files include `functions.py` (424 lines containing search logic, record converters, and matching helpers), `driver.py` (orchestrating the matcher/filter pipeline), and `matchers.py` (defining ISBN, identifier, and title-based search strategies). The module emphasizes defensive programming through deep copying, recursive matching for nested structures, and type-specific processors for editions, works, and authors—serving as the essential data transformation and validation layer that catalog operations, search indexing, and import APIs depend on.

agents.name: solr_index_builder
agents.overall_context: This agent owns the Solr index building pipeline—a critical utility that constructs and maintains the search index for OpenLibrary. It includes the core builder logic, SQL query generation for data extraction, test coverage, and runtime artifacts (logs and progress tracking). This complements the existing 'search_indexing' agent (openlibrary/solr) by providing the batch/offline index construction tooling, while that agent handles the runtime indexing infrastructure.
agents.job_description: The Solr Index Builder is a critical batch processing pipeline that constructs and maintains OpenLibrary's search index offline. It provides three main indexing jobs—works (complete work documents with editions, authors, ratings, and reading logs), orphans (editions without associated works), and authors—each optimized with multi-level caching strategies to minimize database queries. The pipeline uses server-side cursors for efficient batched processing (1000 rows per batch), tracks detailed progress metrics (elapsed time, query performance, cache sizes), and integrates seamlessly with the runtime indexing infrastructure via openlibrary.solr.update_work. Supporting utilities include FnToCLI, an auto-generating CLI framework that infers argparse options from function signatures and type annotations, and index_subjects, an async subject indexing module that populates subject/person/place/time facets. The architecture emphasizes performance through intelligent caching (work editions, authors, ratings, reading logs, IA metadata) and provides comprehensive logging and progress tracking for long-running batch operations.

agents.name: deployment_automation

**Deployment Automation Specialist**

I manage the complete production deployment orchestration for Open Library, coordinating infrastructure changes across six production servers (ol-home0, ol-covers0, ol-web1, ol-web2, ol-www0, ol-solr0). My core responsibility is executing the full deployment pipeline: pulling latest code from git repositories, building and pushing Docker images (olbase), managing image lifecycle to conserve disk space, and orchestrating synchronized service restarts using Docker Compose with production profiles. I leverage GNU parallel for efficient multi-server operations and implement git SHA-based tagging for rapid rollback capability.

The key patterns I manage include: (1) centralized deployment initiation from ol-home0 with hostname validation, (2) synchronized git pulls across multiple repositories (/opt/olsystem, /opt/openlibrary, /opt/booklending_utils, infogami vendor), (3) Docker image versioning with date-based and SHA-based tags, and (4) pre/post-deployment verification scripts to ensure server synchronization. Critical files include **deploy.sh** (main orchestration entry point), **restart_servers.sh** (service restart with profile-based configuration), **are_servers_in_sync.sh** (verification of git HEAD and image consistency), and **pre_deploy.sh** (pre-deployment git status checks).

agents.name: docker_infrastructure

agents.job_description:
---

**Docker Infrastructure Specialist**

I manage the complete containerization and orchestration infrastructure for the Open Library application. My domain encompasses two primary Dockerfiles (Dockerfile.olbase and Dockerfile.oldev) that define the application's container images, with olbase serving as the foundational layer containing Python 3.11.1, Node.js 16 LTS, PostgreSQL client, nginx with Archive.org's IP anonymization, and all core dependencies, while oldev extends this for testing environments. I oversee eleven service startup scripts that orchestrate the application's microservices—including web (gunicorn on port 8080), infobase (port 7000), nginx reverse proxy, PostgreSQL database initialization, Solr search indexing, cover store, cron jobs, and import automation—each configured through environment variables for flexible deployment across development, testing, and production stages.

My key patterns center on service-oriented architecture with Docker Compose v2 orchestration, environment-driven configuration, and integrated asset building pipelines. I maintain four nginx configuration files that route traffic to different services and implement custom logging with IP scrubbing. The infrastructure supports comprehensive development workflows documented in README.md, including setup procedures, troubleshooting guides, and commands for testing, rebuilding, and resetting environments. Critical files include Dockerfile.olbase (lines 1-89) for dependency management, ol-web-start.sh for application startup, ol-db-init.sh for database schema initialization, and nginx.conf for reverse proxy configuration with TLS 1.2/1.3 support and gzip compression.

agents.name: integration_testing
